comments.body:
## Phase 1 RCA — CONFIRMED at runtime (rebar-debug)

The suspicion in the scope note is correct: **this is a wiring job, not new accounting.** The
loop-vs-breadth signal is already computed on the failure path and then thrown away one frame
from the write.

### Root cause 1 (the "computed then discarded" defect)

`usage_log.record()` builds its row from a fixed allowlist,
`_FIELDS = (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, requests)`
(`src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:32`), iterated at `usage_log.py:311-312`. Everything else in the
`usage` dict is silently dropped.

`record_failure()` (`usage_log.py:320`) hands `record()` the FULL `failure_usage()` dict
(`usage_log.py:136-191`), which computes seven further keys — `tool_calls`,
`tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`, `request_limit`,
`tool_calls_limit`, `finish_reason`. **All seven are discarded at the write.**

This violates the module's own cited contract twice over:
- `record_failure`'s docstring (`usage_log.py:338-345`): the failure row "is deliberately the
  SAME shape a successful one has ... Counters come from `failure_usage`, which reads what was
  actually burned".
- `failure_usage`'s docstring (`usage_log.py:150-156`) declares the whole POINT of the
  signature summary: "a run with many calls but few distinct signatures is looping; one with
  many distinct signatures is exploring."

The signal survives only as an ephemeral log line via `format_repetition` (`usage_log.py:237`).

**Discriminating experiment (runtime, offline `FunctionModel` exhaustion run through the real
`PydanticAIRunner`).** Prediction if the root cause is true: `failure_usage()` returns the loop
signal and the FILE row lacks it. Observed:

    failure_usage() COMPUTED: requests=125 tool_calls=125 tool_calls_distinct=1
                              max_consecutive_repeat=125 request_limit=125 tool_calls_limit=250
                              top_repeated_tool_calls=[{read_file:9148ca16, 125}]
    ROW WRITTEN TO DISK:      op/outcome/model/timestamp + input/output/cache_read/
                              cache_write/requests   <- 125 requests, nothing else
    COMPUTED BUT DISCARDED:   finish_reason, max_consecutive_repeat, request_limit,
                              tool_calls, tool_calls_distinct, tool_calls_limit,
                              top_repeated_tool_calls

A textbook 125/1 loop (distinct ratio 0.008) is recorded on disk as indistinguishable from 125
requests of genuine breadth. This is the exact class 70bc's windowed distinct-ratio needs and
cannot get.

### Root cause 2 (why nothing is recorded for a normal gate run)

`record()` no-ops unless `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` names a path (`usage_log.py:295-297`). It is set in
exactly three places — `prompt-eval.yml`, `external-integration.yml`, and the review-bot
service in `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:212`. **A local operator gate run sets none of
them, so it records nothing at all** — which is precisely why answering one question required
four live instrumented runs. Not explainable by root cause 1; a genuinely separate mechanism.

### Root cause 3 (the success path never computes the shape)

`_extract_usage` (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:453-484`, re-exported into `runner.py:50`)
returns exactly five keys and no `tool_calls`. Verified at runtime: the success row is
`requests=1` with no tool-call field. Neither row carries wall-clock duration.

### What IS already persisted (so no second mechanism gets built)

- Plan-review sidecar DOES carry per-call `requests` (`plan_review/sizing.py:292-310`) and a
  `metrics` block with `det_ms`/`llm_ms`/`total_ms`/`llm_calls`
  (`workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:151-177`). No `tool_calls`.
- Completion verdict sidecar carries **no** counts, limits or duration at all
  (`completion_sidecar.py:271-306`).
- Signed attestations carry no run metadata by design — deliberately timestamp-free so
  re-signing is reproducible (`_commands/transition_close.py:129-130`).
- Only `tool_calls` on disk today is the gate-error sidecar, and only on the completion
  bounded-recovery arm (`workflow/completion_recovery.py:255-267`); the other five
  `emit_gate_error` sites pass no diagnostic.

### Legitimacy

- RC1: **`defect`** — violates the module's own cited docstring contract (above).
- RC2/RC3: **`incomplete-implementation`** — cited design authority is
  `docs/llm-framework.md:698-704`, which gives operators tuning advice ("a high recursion limit
  means you're paying for a loop, fix the loop") premised on data the system never records.

Both unlock repair.

### Caller-dependency sweep

`record()`'s only callers are `agent_call.record_call_spend` and `usage_log.record_failure`.
Row consumers (`summarize`, `_read`, `usage_kwargs`) read by `.get(field, 0)` over fixed field
tuples, so extra keys are ignored — adding keys is backward-compatible for every existing
reader. No behavioral dependency on the absence of these fields. Clear to proceed.

comments.body:
# Phase 2 report — FIXED (rebar-debug). Gerrit change 1435.

Phase 1 RCA is in the first comment. This is what changed and the evidence.

## Already captured vs newly persisted

The scope note was right: a WIRING job. `failure_usage()` (`usage_log.py:136-191`) already
reduced a run's messages to the complete loop-vs-breadth signal; `record()` built its row from
`_FIELDS` alone and dropped seven keys one frame from the write. No second mechanism was built —
the success path now calls THE SAME reducer.

| field | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| four token counters + `requests` | persisted | unchanged |
| `tool_calls`, `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`, `request_limit`, `tool_calls_limit`, `finish_reason` | **computed then discarded** | persisted, BOTH paths |
| `duration_s`, `ticket` | did not exist | persisted |
| a gate run with no env var set | **recorded nothing at all** | records to `.rebar/usage.jsonl` |

## Where it lives + retrieval

`REBAR_USAGE_LOG` still wins when set. Unset, a run inside a GATE SESSION appends to
`<repo root>/.rebar/usage.jsonl`. The predicate is the existing fail-closed `in_gate_session()`
that every code-reading gate binds through the one chokepoint `gate_source.gate_read_root`
(`gate_source.py:110`; entered by `plan_review/__init__.py:459` and `completion.py:485`) — no new
plumbing. Outside a gate session with the var unset, `record()` still writes nothing at all.

    python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize .rebar/usage.jsonl

## PROOF — a real gate run, never instrumented

`REBAR_USAGE_LOG` confirmed unset (`env | grep -c` -> 0), then `rebar review-plan aec1-...`:

    plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  failed  requests=0  tool_calls=0  duration=185.6s
    ticket-digest                      ok      requests=1  tool_calls=0  duration=6.1s
    overlap-judge                      ok      requests=1  tool_calls=0  duration=4.7s
    overlap-judge                      ok      requests=1  tool_calls=0  duration=17.2s
    overlap-judge                      ok      requests=1  tool_calls=0  duration=4.7s

Row 1 in full: step=prerequisite_verify, model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6,
request_limit=125, tool_calls_limit=250, tool_calls_distinct=0, max_consecutive_repeat=0,
top_repeated_tool_calls=[], duration_s=185.6. **A FAILED call that burned three minutes and
previously left no trace of any kind.** `summarize` folds it, priced:
`| **total** | **4** | **13014** | **942** | **1796** | **1796** | **3** | **$0.0412** |`
`git status` stays clean — `.rebar/*` is already gitignored.

## RED evidence + mutation check

`tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py` was written FIRST and held OUT of the fix
subagent's working tree. RED for the right reasons (not import errors):
`KeyError: 'tool_calls'` (exhaustion), `KeyError: 'tool_calls'` (success),
`KeyError: 'tool_calls_distinct'`, `KeyError: 'duration_s'`,
`AttributeError: _repo_root_for_default_sink` -> 6 failed, 1 passed.
Then GREEN 7/7 against an oracle the fixer never saw.

Two defect-seeded mutations, each re-introducing a confirmed root cause:
- remove the `_SHAPE_FIELDS` write in `record()` -> **4 failed**, same original KeyErrors
- disable the gate default sink -> **1 failed** ("a gate run recorded nothing without
  REBAR_USAGE_LOG")
Both restored to 7/7. The tests that stayed green under mutation 1 test different mechanisms,
so the oracle discriminates rather than blanket-failing.

## BOTH paths write — the axis varies

Three fixtures: `_ok_model` (success), `_breadth_model` (all-distinct, terminates),
`_looping_model` (one repeated signature, runs to budget exhaustion).
`test_a_loop_and_a_breadth_run_are_separable_from_the_record_alone` asserts the ratio separates
them FROM THE DURABLE RECORD ALONE: breadth 5/5 = 1.00 vs loop 1/125 = 0.008. The four live
measured examples reproduce from the same two fields (238/258 = 0.922 healthy; 76/257 = 0.296,
167/270 = 0.619, 135/264 = 0.511 pathological).
`test_a_non_gate_run_still_writes_nothing_when_unset` is the control in the OTHER direction —
without it the gate-sink test would pass for the trivial reason that everything writes.

## Coordination with 70bc — field naming

I invented no vocabulary. The record uses the names `_repetition_summary()` already mints:
`tool_calls`, `tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`. 70bc
should adopt these rather than either of us minting a second set.

LIMITATION, stated rather than papered over: these are WHOLE-RUN counts. They reproduce every
ratio in the four measured examples (the stated minimum), but a WINDOWED ratio at an arbitrary
window cannot be recomputed from aggregates, because the signature SEQUENCE is not stored
(deliberately — it would grow the row without bound). If 70bc pins a window size, the natural
extension is to emit per-window ratios at that size from the same `_repetition_summary` seam.

## Siblings (Step 7, both axes)

CONSTRUCT sweep (class: a fixed allowlist admitting the LIMIT and dropping the MEASUREMENT).
Swept every allowlist constant under `src/rebar`, each hit confirmed semantically not by string
match. Exactly one live sibling: `failure.py:82-96` `_ALLOWED_FIELDS` carries `request_limit` and
`tool_calls_limit` but neither `requests` nor `tool_calls`. `_FIELDS`/`_TOKEN_FIELDS` narrowings
are deliberate and correct; the parsing/validation allowlists are not this class.

PARITY sweep (rule: a durable record of a gate call must carry what it CONSUMED, not only what it
was allowed to consume). usage-log JSONL = FIXED. Gate-error sidecar = MISSING (and 5 of 6
`emit_gate_error` sites pass no diagnostic at all). Completion verdict sidecar = MISSING (no
counts, no duration — while plan-review's already has `requests` + a `metrics` block, so the two
gates are asymmetric and the completion gate is the blind one). Signed attestation manifest =
N/A WITH REASON: deliberately timestamp-free so re-signing reproduces
(`transition_close.py:129-130`), so a run-varying metric structurally cannot live there.

DISPOSITION: every MISSING slot filed as **df94-66ba-dbf8-4ac1**, linked `discovered_from` this
ticket. Not folded in here because `_ALLOWED_FIELDS` is a SANITIZATION boundary — widening it is a
privacy decision deserving its own review, not a ride-along on a telemetry fix.

## Residual risk

- **Unbounded growth.** `.rebar/usage.jsonl` is append-only and nothing prunes it. ACCEPTED and
  documented (append-only, gitignored, never read back by rebar, safe to delete any time) — the
  same caveat `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:200-211` already records for the review-bot sink.
  Rotation would be new machinery on a bug fix.
- **`ticket` is absent in practice for plan-review's own ops.** The field is wired and tested end
  to end, but plan-review builds its `RunRequest`s with an empty `target`, so there is no
  `ticket_id` and `record()` correctly omits the key (visible in the real rows above). ACCEPTED;
  populating `target` at those call sites is a separate change.
- **First-run leak-guard interaction.** If a gate runs CONCURRENTLY with the test suite, the
  first-ever creation of `.rebar/usage.jsonl` is a new REPO_ROOT entry and the suite's leak guard
  flags whichever test is in flight. Only on first creation; appends are not new entries. ACCEPTED,
  recorded here so the next reader is not misled — it cost me a false conclusion (below).

## A false conclusion this session, and the controls that caught it

I first saw a live gate run write nothing and nearly reported the fix broken. Three controls
corrected it: (1) `rebar review-code` is DISABLED in this project, so that run made zero LLM calls
— a vacuous experiment; (2) plain untracked control files placed in `.rebar/` vanished within 30s
TOO, proving the deletion was environmental (the suite's leak guard `rmtree`), not my code; (3) the
first full-suite run's 18 errors included four reading literally "Test moved the repo HEAD
(34998a2ca8 -> 902ee42663)" — MY OWN COMMIT, made while the suite ran — and the rest were my manual
probe files. Re-running exactly those gate tests cleanly: **121 passed**.

## Files changed (Gerrit 1435)

    src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py   _SHAPE_FIELDS, shape_only(), run_shape alias, _resolve_sink()/
                                 _repo_root_for_default_sink(), duration_s+ticket on record()
                                 and record_failure()                                  [754 LOC]
    src/rebar/llm/runner.py      success-path shape via the SAME reducer; duration+ticket [785]
    src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py  record_call_spend forwards duration_s/ticket            [189]
    docs/llm-framework.md        run-shape fields, default gate sink, retrieval, lifecycle
    tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py   NEW — the held-out RED->GREEN oracle

No existing test modified, weakened, skipped or xfailed (`git diff --stat -- tests/` empty). No new
dependency (`typing.Any` is stdlib; `rebar.config` / `rebar.llm.config` are lazy in-tree imports).
All modules under the 800 cap. lint = 0, typecheck = 0.

OVERLAP NOTE for the agent on c827/70bc: `agent_call.py` is touched (7 lines, two optional kwargs
forwarded). `structured_run.py`'s `failure_usage` call sites are UNTOUCHED — which is exactly why
`failure_usage` was ALIASED (`run_shape = failure_usage`) rather than renamed. `workflow/runs.py`
is untouched.

Clean re-run: `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q`
-> **1 failed, 10550 passed, 38 skipped, 4 errors** in 618.88s, exit **1**.

Both categories are accounted for, neither is this change:

**The 4 errors are self-inflicted.** All four read literally

**Verification that IS attributable:** `make lint` = 0, `make typecheck` = 0 locally, and Gerrit

comments.body:
## Plan-review gate PASSED and CERTIFIED — plus hard data on the sonnet-4-6 grammar timeout

`rebar review-plan aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86` -> **exit 0, verdict PASS**, and
`--status` -> `{"ok": true, "verdict": "certified", "verified_at_sha":
"4b5a7bcd4adf744d96ba98fcd953afa3c37d780e", "signed_at": 1785956593907797000}`.
Obtained with **`REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL` UNSET**, on stock `sonnet-4-6`, with **no `--force`**.

### Evidence bearing on rebar ticket 895c (sonnet-4-6 native-structured-output grammar timeout)

This is the first question of its kind answerable **by query instead of by re-running**, which is
the whole point of this ticket. Source: `.rebar/usage.jsonl`, 73 recorded calls across
plan-review runs 3-5.

**The 185s signature is REAL and reproducible — 895c's root cause is corroborated:**

    17:36:11  plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  dur=185.6s  requests=0  sonnet-4-6  FAILED
    18:10:23  plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  dur=185.7s  requests=0  sonnet-4-6  FAILED
    18:37:06  plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  dur=185.6s  requests=0  sonnet-4-6  FAILED
    19:03:10  plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  dur=185.6s  requests=0  sonnet-4-6  FAILED

Four occurrences, all on the same step, all 185.6-185.7s, all `requests=0` — no model request
ever completed, exactly what a pre-response 400 looks like. That is a tight, deterministic
fingerprint and it matches 895c's described ~180s grammar-compilation timeout.

**But it does NOT cause INDETERMINATE, and does NOT block certification.** The attestation was
signed at **19:03:13 UTC** and the failure above is at **19:03:10 — three seconds earlier, inside
the very run that passed and signed.** The step degrades; the review still completes and signs.

**So "retrying is futile without the env var" is falsified here:** a certified PASS was earned
without it. Recommend 895c narrow the claim from "the run cannot be verified" to "this one step
degrades", unless there is a separate case where it is genuinely fatal.

**What the verdict actually tracked was the plan findings, not the timeout.** The 185s failure
was CONSTANT across runs 3, 4 and 5, while the verdict moved:

    run 3: blocking 0, advisory 1, indeterminate 14  -> INDETERMINATE   (185s failure present)
    run 4: blocking 0, advisory 0, indeterminate  3  -> INDETERMINATE   (185s failure present)
    run 5: blocking 0, advisory 0, indeterminate  0  -> PASS + CERTIFIED (185s failure present)

A constant cannot explain a variable. The indeterminate count fell 14 -> 3 -> 0 tracking exactly
the findings addressed each round (declaring `run_shape`/`shape_only` as NEW work rather than
citing them as pre-existing was the single biggest one — plan-review reads the ATTESTED
`gerrit/main` snapshot, where a change's own new symbols legitimately do not exist yet). So the
plan edits were not a red herring on this ticket; they were the operative variable.

**A second, DISTINCT failure mode also shows up**, which is not the grammar timeout and should
not be folded into 895c:

    18:17:37 / 18:23:03 / 18:28:45 / 18:43:09 / 18:48:24  overlap-judge  312-381s  requests=3  FAILED

Real requests completed (`requests=3`) and durations are 312-381s, not ~185s. Different shape,
different cause. Overall across the three runs: 64 ok / 9 failed = 12.3% call failure rate.

**Caveat:** these are 4 samples of the timeout on one step of one ticket, from one host. They
corroborate the fingerprint; they do not establish the mechanism (I did not capture the Bedrock
400 body). 895c's schema-complexity analysis remains the mechanism of record.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Addendum — the sonnet/bedrock failure family has TWO shapes, split by botocore version

Extends the previous comment. A second failure shape exists that my runs never hit, and the
`duration_s` field this ticket adds is what makes the two distinguishable by query rather than by
re-running:

- **Server-side, ~185s** — native structured output times out compiling the grammar. Seen here
  4x on `plan-review-prerequisite-verifier`, `requests=0`, sonnet-4-6. Degrades that one step.
- **Client-side, ~0.0s** — an OLDER botocore rejects the request before it is sent:
  `Parameter validation failed: Unknown parameter in input: "outputConfig"`. Independent of
  schema size, so it hits EVERY native call including trivial-class ones, and it fails silently.

**Measured version boundary on this host:**

    this worktree (.venv, provisioned by `make worktree`)  botocore 1.43.62
    main checkout /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.venv            botocore 1.40.61

**My recorded data confirms which side I was on** (73 calls, plan-review runs 3-5):

    failed calls with duration_s < 1.0s   : 0        <- no client-side rejects at all
    ticket-digest (722 B, trivial class)  : 4/4 OK, 6.1s / 6.9s / 6.7s / 7.2s, haiku-4-5

`ticket-digest` is exactly the call measured failing at 0.0s on botocore 1.40.61, and it
succeeded every time here. So the failure is **checkout-dependent, not ticket-dependent**: gates
run from the main checkout hit the silent client-side variant; gates run from a `make worktree`
worktree hit the 185s server-side one.

Practical consequence for anyone reading this ticket later: `make worktree` (which provisions a
fresh venv) is why this ticket's gate runs worked without any model-override stopgap. The real
fix for the main checkout is upgrading botocore, not only overriding the model class.

Credit: the two-shape split and the client-side reproduction are the coordinator's measurement on
rebar ticket 895c; recorded here because the previous comment would otherwise read as if ~185s
were the only failure mode.

compiled_state.description:
# LLM gate runs record no per-run request or tool-call counts, so the gates cannot be tuned

## The gap

**Nothing durably records how many model requests or tool calls a gate run consumed.** There is no
usage log on disk, and the audit sidecar carries criteria and citations but no request/tool-call
counts. Established while investigating rebar ticket c827: the control-group question
"how many of the 240 available requests did the epics that closed cleanly actually use?" **could not
be answered from the store at all.**

## Why this matters — it is why the same bug recurred six times

The completion gate's step budget has been raised **five times** across its history
(the history sweep on rebar ticket c827), a hard tool-call cap was proposed and deferred
(rebar ticket 7c58) then proposed and rejected (rebar ticket b2bb), and the verifier's own creating
epic was force-closed citing the limitation as "documented". **Every one of those decisions was made
without spend data**, because the data was never recorded.

The cost of that absence is measurable: answering a single question about this gate required **four
live instrumented runs at ~20-50 minutes each**, re-deriving numbers that should have been a query.
And the tuning advice the docs give (the loop-tuning advice in `docs/llm-framework.md`'s completion-verifier
section — "a high recursion limit means you're paying for a loop, fix the loop") is unactionable, because nothing tells an operator whether
they are paying for a loop or for breadth.

This is the same **"computed then discarded"** shape as two sibling defects: the repetition
diagnostic that `interpret_failure` builds and `raise_completion_workflow_failure` drops
(rebar ticket c827), and the deterministic child-closure proof collapsed to a boolean
(rebar ticket 6ec8). The value is produced and thrown away one frame from the surface.

## Scope note

`usage_log` machinery already exists in-tree (e.g. `usage_log.failure_usage`,
`usage_log.capture_attempt_messages`), and `RunContext` exposes `.usage` inside the tool-filter predicate (`agent_call.py:70-71`), though that predicate currently reads only `run_ctx.run_step` — the usage actually reachable at record time comes from `failure_usage`, not from that predicate.
**Establish what is already captured before adding anything** — the likely defect is that the data is
captured and not persisted, in which case this is a wiring job, not new accounting. Do not build a
second, parallel usage mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

Each line is one independently verifiable deliverable.

- [ ] a gate run persists the model requests it consumed
- [ ] a gate run persists the tool calls it consumed
- [ ] a gate run persists the `request_limit` it ran under
- [ ] a gate run persists the `tool_calls_limit` it ran under
- [ ] a gate run persists the step name
- [ ] a gate run persists the ticket id when the caller supplies one
- [ ] a gate run persists wall-clock duration
- [ ] the FAILURE path records all of the above (a run that exhausts its budget or errors is
      exactly when the numbers are needed, and is the case most likely to be missed)
- [ ] the SUCCESS path records all of the above, so a clean run is usable as a control group
- [ ] the distinct-vs-total tool-call-signature counts are recorded, so a LOOP is distinguishable
      from genuine BREADTH after the fact without re-running
- [ ] a gate run persists the worst-consecutive-repeat count
- [ ] a gate run persists `finish_reason`, recorded for triage but deliberately not rendered
- [ ] the record is produced by an ordinary gate run with no env var set
- [ ] the record is produced with no instrumentation added to the run
- [ ] the named retrieval command RENDERS the total tool-call count in its own output
- [ ] the named retrieval command RENDERS the distinct tool-call count in its own output
- [ ] that rendering is proven by pasting the rendered output, never a raw JSONL line
- [ ] the retrieval command's existing token/cost table is unchanged, pinned by a test
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` points operators at the new rendered command output
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` documents the new `.rebar/usage.jsonl` artifact
- [ ] a test pins that the counts are WRITTEN on the success path
- [ ] a test pins that the counts are WRITTEN on the exhaustion path
- [ ] a test pins that a gate run writes with NO env var set (the positive gate-sink case)
- [ ] a test pins that a NON-gate run still writes nothing with no env var set (the control)
- [ ] no second parallel usage mechanism is introduced where the existing one can be wired

### Explicitly OUT of scope (recorded so it is not mistaken for a gap)

**The record carries WHOLE-RUN aggregates only.** It does NOT carry the ordered tool-call
signature SEQUENCE. The windowed distinct-ratio that rebar ticket 70bc establishes is a
trailing-window set cardinality, which provably needs that ordered sequence, so it is NOT
computable from this record — only the whole-run ratio is. That whole-run ratio does reproduce
every measured example (238/258 = 0.92 healthy; 76/257 = 0.30, 167/270 = 0.62, 135/264 = 0.51
pathological), which is the discrimination this ticket needs. Storing the sequence would grow
each row without bound, so if 70bc pins a window size the natural follow-up is to emit per-window
ratios at that size from the same `_repetition_summary` seam. Flagged for 70bc, not done here.

**`finish_reason` is a raw provider passthrough with no vocabulary owned by rebar.** It is
recorded for triage (it is what distinguishes a length-stop from a tool-stop when reading a
failed row) and is deliberately NOT rendered by the retrieval command, precisely because its
value set is the provider's and would otherwise read as a rebar-defined enum.

## Fix plan — wire the EXISTING mechanism, add nothing parallel

Root cause (confirmed at runtime; full RCA in the first comment): `usage_log.record()` builds its
row from the single allowlist `_FIELDS` (`usage_log.py:32`, iterated at `:311`), so the seven
further keys `failure_usage()` (`usage_log.py:136-191`) already computes — `tool_calls`,
`tool_calls_distinct`, `max_consecutive_repeat`, `top_repeated_tool_calls`, `request_limit`,
`tool_calls_limit`, `finish_reason` — are **computed and then discarded at the write**.

### Step 1 — `record()` stops discarding, and two NEW names are introduced

All three of the following are NEW work; none exists in the tree today:

- **`_SHAPE_FIELDS`** (new module constant) — a second explicit allowlist holding those seven
  keys, written by `record()` **only when present** in the `usage` dict. Absent means "not
  measured"; defaulting to `0` would make a shapeless caller assert the falsehood "this run used
  no tools", which later aggregates would sum as fact. An explicit allowlist, not `**usage`
  passthrough, so this module keeps owning its durable schema.
- **`run_shape`** (new module-level ALIAS) — `run_shape = failure_usage`. A thin outcome-neutral
  name for the EXISTING reducer, introduced because the success path now calls the same function
  and a success-path call spelled `failure_usage(...)` would tell a reader the opposite of the
  truth. `failure_usage` is NOT renamed: it has live call sites in `llm/structured_run.py` that
  another agent is editing concurrently, so renaming would collide.
- **`shape_only(shape)`** (new function) — returns exactly the `_SHAPE_FIELDS` subset of a
  `run_shape` result. It exists so a caller merging the shape into its own usage dict need not
  reach into the private field tuple, and so the token totals the reducer also computes are
  dropped rather than overwriting the provider's authoritative figures.

`record()` also gains `duration_s` and `ticket` as explicit optional keyword arguments.

### Step 2 — the SUCCESS path, field by field

`record_call_spend` (`agent_call.py`) receives neither the limits nor the call start time, so the
plumbing is stated explicitly rather than left implicit. **The reducer is called in `runner.py`,
NOT inside `record_call_spend`** — the runner is the frame that holds all three missing inputs:

- `runner.py`, on the success path, calls
  `usage_log.run_shape(run_messages, request_limit=req_limit, tool_calls_limit=max(8, eff_max_iter))`.
  `req_limit` and `eff_max_iter` are already locals there (from `build_usage_limits`), and
  `run_messages` is already populated on the success path because `capture_attempt_messages`
  extends the sink from its `finally`, not from an `except` (verified at runtime).
- **`request_limit` / `tool_calls_limit` reach the row because they are ARGUMENTS to that call
  and the reducer echoes them into its own result** — that is the whole mechanism, and it is why
  no new parameter is needed on `record_call_spend` for them.
- `usage_log.shape_only(...)` filters that result to `_SHAPE_FIELDS`, which `runner.py` merges
  into `usage`. Deliberately NOT the reducer's token totals: those are message-derived
  approximations and must never overwrite `_extract_usage`'s authoritative provider figures.
- **`duration_s`** — computed in `runner.py` as `time.monotonic() - _t0` (the existing call-start
  marker) and passed as a NEW optional kwarg on `record_call_spend`, which forwards it to
  `record`.
- **`ticket`** — `req.target.get("ticket_id")`, passed the same way. Absent when the caller set no
  target, and then omitted from the row.
- The failure path passes `duration_s`/`ticket` through `record_failure` as keyword-only
  arguments with defaults, leaving its existing positional signature unbroken.
- BOTH paths are wrapped in a swallow-and-log guard, not only the success one: telemetry must
  never break the call it measures. On the success path `runner.py` wraps the shape capture; on
  the FAILURE path `record_failure` already wraps its ENTIRE body — shape capture, the
  `duration_s`/`ticket` forwarding, and the `record()` write alike — and that is load-bearing
  there, because its caller is an `except` block whose one job is to re-raise the provider's
  exception unchanged: an error escaping telemetry would REPLACE that exception and destroy the
  real diagnosis.

### Step 3 — gate runs record with no env var set, and WHERE the root comes from

`record()` resolves its sink through a new `_resolve_sink()`: `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` (explicit, still
wins) -> else, **iff `in_gate_session()`**, `<repo root>/.rebar/usage.jsonl` when that directory
already exists -> else no-op exactly as today.

**The repo root is obtained by a new `_repo_root_for_default_sink()`, which calls
`rebar.config.repo_root()` — the git toplevel of the PROCESS CWD.** This is deliberately NOT the
gate's active code root. In attested mode `gate_read_root` points the code root at a throwaway
temp snapshot; writing the usage log there would produce a record that vanishes with the
snapshot and is unretrievable from the operator's checkout. Resolving from CWD instead puts the
row in the checkout the operator is standing in, which is the only place they can read it from.
Verified empirically: a real attested `review-plan` wrote its rows to the working checkout's
`.rebar/usage.jsonl`, not into a snapshot dir.

`in_gate_session()` is the existing fail-closed marker every code-reading gate binds through the
single chokepoint `gate_source.gate_read_root` (`gate_source.py:110`, entered by
`plan_review/__init__.py:459` and `completion.py:485`), so this needs no new plumbing. Imported
via `rebar.llm.config`, not `gate_context` directly, because `test_gate_context_seam.py` forbids
the latter for every module under `src/`. Every non-gate caller stays byte-identical, preserving
the module's no-op-when-unset guarantee.

**Lifecycle of the new artifact.** `.rebar/usage.jsonl` is append-only, git-ignored, disposable
local state: rebar never reads it back (only the operator and `summarize` do), so it may be
truncated or deleted at any time with no loss of function. Nothing prunes it, so it grows with
every gate run; the documented guidance is to delete it after a measurement, or point
`REBAR_USAGE_LOG` at a per-session path for a clean window. No rotation is implemented, matching
the existing caveat already recorded for the long-lived review-bot sink in
`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:200-211`. Each row is one single-append complete line, so
concurrent gate runs interleave rows without corrupting one.

### Step 4 — the retrieval command must RENDER the new fields

`summarize()` today folds only the token `_FIELDS`, so a row can carry `tool_calls=125,
tool_calls_distinct=1` and the operator running the named command still sees only token counters.
**A fix that leaves the signal written but not displayed reproduces the very "computed then
discarded" pattern this ticket exists to remove, one layer further out.** So a new
`_run_shape_section()` helper renders a `Run shape (loop vs breadth)` table — per op: calls,
total tool calls, distinct, the distinct/total ratio, worst consecutive repeat, and both limits.
An op that made no tool calls prints an em dash, never `0.000`, because no measurement is not a
perfect loop.

Constraint: the existing token/cost table is **unchanged** and the new section is APPENDED, never
merged in as extra columns — that table feeds `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` on the two billable weekly
jobs and several existing tests assert on it. Rows carrying no shape fields (every pre-aec1 row)
are skipped, and an all-shapeless log renders no section at all, so old logs summarize exactly as
they did.

### Step 5 — documentation

`docs/llm-framework.md` is updated in the same change: the `usage_log` section documents the
run-shape fields, `duration_s`/`ticket`, the default gate sink and its lifecycle, and shows the
rendered `Run shape` table with both poles. This is what makes the existing tuning advice at
the loop-tuning advice in `docs/llm-framework.md` ("a high recursion limit means you're paying for a loop, fix the
loop") actionable for the first time — that advice is the motivation for this ticket, so leaving
it without a pointer to the new output would leave the motivating gap open.

## Retrieval

    python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize .rebar/usage.jsonl

## Testing

    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q
    make lint && make typecheck

`tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py` drives the REAL runner offline (`FunctionModel` +
`ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS=False`, the established pattern in `test_usage_log_failed_calls.py`) and
reads the written FILE, varying the path axis three ways: `_ok_model` (success), `_breadth_model`
(all-distinct exploration, terminates), `_looping_model` (one repeated signature, runs to budget
exhaustion). Named tests:

- exhaustion path: `tool_calls`, `request_limit`, `tool_calls_limit` are written
- success path: `tool_calls`/`tool_calls_distinct` are written, and a SEPARATE test asserts
  `request_limit`, `tool_calls_limit` and `duration_s` are present, so the Step-2 plumbing cannot
  silently regress to failure-path-only
- the recorded distinct-vs-total ratio separates a loop from breadth FROM THE RECORD ALONE
- POSITIVE gate-sink case: a gate run writes with no env var set (the `.rebar` root is pinned via
  `_repo_root_for_default_sink` so the test needs no chdir)
- CONTROL: a NON-gate run still writes nothing with the env var unset, so the positive test above
  cannot pass for the trivial reason that everything writes
- rendering: `summarize()` output CONTAINS the tool-call and distinct counts and reads as a loop
- invariance: the existing token/cost table is unchanged, and a pre-aec1 log with no shape fields
  renders with no run-shape section at all
